title: Operations & Administration VA | Electrical Trades, SOP Building
description:
Application form:



Role Overview



Candidates with strong, verifiable operations or EA experience, ideally from a trades or construction business, and demonstrable SOP-building skills will be prioritised for this role.



An electrical business needs a self-directed, operations-first VA to take ownership of business administration, job management and SOP documentation. The role is operations and administration-led, not marketing-led — social media and website work remain part of the role, but at a scheduling and execution level, with content strategy handled by an external specialist. This is a strong, self-directed operator role: both directors want someone who takes a task, owns it completely, and delivers without needing to be followed up — someone who pushes back, asks good questions, and suggests a better way when they see one.



The role starts at 20 hours per week (4 hours per day, Monday to Friday), with the expectation this grows to full-time reasonably quickly as more tasks are handed over. A broader goal is a fully documented, less founder-dependent business that could run — or be sold — without day-to-day founder involvement by the end of 2027.



What You’ll Own



Operations, Administration & SOP-Building (Primary Focus)



General business administration support: assisting with quotes, invoicing for jobs, and timesheet administration in preparation for payroll

Contribute to building a fully documented, less founder-dependent business

Build out SOPs directly in Asana as processes are established, breaking each task down with the responsible person, day, and expected duration



Job Management (Katipolt)



Manage the back end of the job management platform: job cards, materials uploads, scheduling support, and related workflow

Draft invoices on job completion for maintenance and smaller jobs

Support quoting in the platform

Assist with materials coordination, including checking supplier deliveries and confirming gear is ready for upcoming jobs



Process Documentation



Document new workflows and processes as they’re refined and established — building the SOP library directly off live processes

Store and link all SOPs in Asana, accessible via the mobile app so field-based staff can reference them

Set a quarterly SOP review cadence to keep documentation accurate as the business evolves



 & Customer Communication



Monitor the inbox for customer replies to the business’s automated follow-up sequence, respond where appropriate, and close the loop in the system

Support customer communication throughout the job lifecycle, from initial enquiry through to job completion and follow-up

Manage customer comms within the job platform where possible



Social Media & Website (Scheduling-Level, Not Strategist-Level)



Receive approved content and manage scheduling and light repurposing (e.g. turning a video into a carousel or still-image post) across Instagram,
 and 
 using Meta Business Suite

Update and maintain the WordPress website with minor copy and photo changes as directed — no major redesign or SEO landing-page work required



Business Development & Lead Pipeline



Build and manage a lead pipeline in Asana, moving prospects through stages from initial enquiry to converted client

Manage and improve the quote follow-up process, ensuring no opportunities go cold without contact

Develop and document customer journey touchpoints: enquiry, quote, job commencement, completion, and follow-up/review request

Support outreach and marketing materials as directed



Task & Communication Management



Send a morning WhatsApp message each day with planned priorities

Send an end-of-day
 report covering tasks completed, work in progress, and items requiring attention or approval

Manage the Asana task board across daily, weekly and monthly cadences

Record training calls and use the recordings, plus AI tools, to generate SOP drafts

Participate in regular video calls, including impromptu calls while a director is on the road



What We’re Looking For



Experience



Strong general business administration or EA background, with trades or construction industry exposure strongly preferred

Experience with business process documentation or SOP creation, ideally including breaking tasks into responsibility, cadence and time-per-task

Experience with job management, CRM or trades platforms (Simpro, ServiceM8, Tradify or WunderBuild experience is highly transferable)

Experience drafting invoices, supporting quoting processes, or managing job administration in a service business



Technical Proficiency (Core, Non-Negotiable)



Asana: experience or strong ability to set up and manage task boards, project pipelines and linked SOPs

Microsoft 365/Teams: comfortable with Outlook
, Teams video and associated tools

Confident, fast learner on job management or trades platforms

AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT): genuine, proactive curiosity, not just baseline familiarity — actively pushes their own use of these tools rather than waiting to be shown

Strong written English for professional, client-facing communications



Technical Proficiency (Nice-to-Have)



Instagram and
 scheduling and 
 via Meta Business Suite

LinkedIn page-building experience from a low base

WordPress: minor content and photo updates; SEO/landing-page skills are a bonus

Xero experience is valuable but not mandatory for day one



Communication & Independence



Proactive, not passive — raises questions, confirms understanding, and flags issues before they become problems

Earns trust quickly with busy, selective directors

Confident enough to suggest a better way and push back constructively

Comfortable on frequent video calls, including impromptu check-ins



Organisational Skills



Manages multiple concurrent workstreams (admin, job platform,
 follow-up, SOP creation, light social scheduling) without dropping the ball

Strong self-directed time management within a 4-hour daily shift

Captures tasks, ideas and follow-up items in Asana unprompted



Non-Negotiables



Demonstrable, verifiable experience — real work samples and portfolio evidence are required, not just a strong interview

Consistent performance under sustained, low-supervision conditions, week after week — not just in the first few weeks

Process-minded: sees a repeatable task and thinks about how to document it, who owns it, and how long it should take

Comfortable with ambiguity — many processes are still being built in real time, and the VA helps create them, not just follow them

Treats every output — a caption, a quote, a drafted invoice — as representing an established, 19-year business

Fast learner on new platforms, particularly the job management system and Asana



Working Arrangements



Starts at 20 hours per week (4 hours per day, Monday to Friday), with a realistic path to full-time as more tasks are handed over

Regular video calls, including impromptu check-ins while a director is on the road



Why This Role



Genuine ownership of operations and SOP-building in a business actively working to become less founder-dependent

Real trust extended quickly to someone who proves they can be handed something and not need chasing

A business actively building AI into how it works, with room to bring your own ideas and curiosity

Growth-oriented environment with a clear path to more responsibility as the role and the business evolve



How to Apply



To be considered, please complete this form and include a short video introduction, along with verifiable work samples or portfolio evidence. It helps us shortlist quickly:

title: Children's Coloring Book Illustrator / Vector Artist — Ongoing Projects
description:
Job Type: Freelance / Project-Based, Potential Long-Term Work  

Initial Paid Test: $20 USD



We are launching Melzoomi, a new children's creative brand specializing in giant peel-and-stick coloring wall murals.



We are looking for a talented, imaginative illustrator who can create original black-and-white coloring artwork for children ages 3–8.



Our designs will feature exciting worlds such as underwater adventures, dinosaurs, magical kingdoms, imaginative cities, and enchanted forests.



What We're Looking For



- Experience creating children's coloring books, activity pages, or similar illustrations

- Strong creativity and character design skills

- Clean, smooth black outlines with large, open coloring areas

- Excellent composition and attention to detail

- Proficiency in Adobe Illustrator or comparable vector software

- Ability to deliver original, editable vector artwork

- Good communication and ability to follow creative briefs



Our Ideal Style



Playful, imaginative, charming, and engaging without being overly complicated or crowded. We want illustrations children will be excited to color and parents will be happy to display.



Paid Test Assignment



We will select up to six applicants to complete a small, paid illustration test.



Each selected applicant will receive the same creative brief and $20 USD upon completion of the agreed assignment.



The test will involve designing a 12" × 12" sample section of an underwater-themed coloring mural, not an entire finished mural.



Long-Term Opportunity



We plan to launch multiple mural collections and expand into additional creative products. The selected illustrator may receive ongoing assignments as the brand grows.



How to Apply — Please Read Carefully



You MUST attach 2–3 examples of your own artwork that are directly relevant to this position.



We specifically want to see:

- Black-and-white children's coloring illustrations

- Coloring book pages or activity illustrations

- Original character illustrations with clean outlines



Do not send only a portfolio link. You are welcome to include your full portfolio as additional information, but we should not have to search through it to find relevant examples.



Please also include:



1. The illustration software you use.

2. Whether you create editable vector artwork.

3. Your typical pricing for illustration projects.

4. Your availability for ongoing freelance work.



Start your application with the word MELZOOMI so we know you have read the full posting.



Applications without relevant artwork samples attached or directly included may not be considered.



We look forward to seeing your creativity!

title: Executive & Personal Assistant | Business Management
description:
Executive & Personal Assistant | Business Management

Company: Coastal Sunset Management

Role Type: Part-Time (approx. 3–5 hours/week) | Long-Term Remote

Compensation: $3–$5 / hour (commensurate with experience)

About the Role

At Coastal Sunset Management, we oversee a portfolio of residential and vacation rental properties across Hawaii, California and Florida, alongside related private business holdings.

We are seeking a seasoned, highly proactive Senior Executive & Personal Assistant to directly support our executive leadership. Working alongside our established back-office management team, your primary mandate is end-to-end ownership: managing details, follow-ups, vendor relationships, and systems so leadership can remain focused on strategy, asset management, and time management.  We are needing someone who can continually follow up with vendors/projects until there done; not stopping after 2 calls with a immense strength of follow-through. If something is still pending, you keep it visible, follow up again, change the communication method when needed, and escalate only when a decision is required. This assistant is comfortable calling vendors, asking for updates, tracking deadlines, and let management be when the task is actually completed.

This Assistant needs to be assertive and gets the vendors in the project to finish their work.

We prefer an experienced professional with experience supporting executives, founders, or business owners. title: AI Production Lead
description:
# AI Production Lead



## About us



We help technology companies win the hardest audience in the world: technical practitioners. Developers, DevOps engineers, security teams. People who ignore marketing and adopt products on merit. Our clients include GitHub, Adobe, Okta, Dynatrace, and Comcast, alongside some of the most exciting funded startups in developer tools and infrastructure.



We're a small, senior, fully remote team, and we're building something unusual: a consulting firm that runs on its own AI platform. Our internal system encodes how we think (our methodology, our client knowledge, our production workflows) into agents that do real work. AI is the operating system of the company.



We're now scaling our productized services, which cover content, video, and market intelligence for clients. We need a technical operator who can run that engine, make it better, keep every client on track, and tell us what the data says.



## The role



You'll sit at the center of how our work gets made. Our strategists d
 what needs to exist: a set of blog posts for a client, a batch of videos, a refreshed metrics dashboard. You make it exist, producing through our AI agents, checking quality, keeping every delivery moving, and keeping the data our systems depend on accurate and fresh.



You'll also build and improve the agents themselves. When an agent produces weak output, you dig into the prompt, the context, the workflow, or the data feeding it, and you fix the system so the next hundred outputs are better. Over time, you'll own a growing share of how our platform actually works.



You'll be the person who holds the whole client picture in your head. At any given time we might have eight clients with work in flight: a blog series for one, a video batch for another, a dashboard refresh for a third, a rush request from a fourth. You'll know where each one stands, what's due when, what "good" looks like for that specific client (their voice, their audience, their standards, what they've pushed back on before), and what to prioritize when everything lands at once. Our strategists set direction. You make sure nothing falls through the cracks and that every client gets work that feels made for them.



You'll be our first reader of the numbers, too. Client metrics, content performance, pipeline health, agent quality. You'll review this data regularly, spot the trends and anomalies, and come to the team with a point of view: what's happening, why you think it's happening, and what we should do about it.



This is not a content-mill job and it's not an admin job. You'll work inside a sophisticated AI platform most companies won't have for years, produce work for some of the biggest names in tech, and be trained directly by the people who built the methodology.



The scope grows with you. The two people you'll work with daily both started in execution roles and now lead major parts of the company. We invest heavily in the people we hire, and mentorship is how we operate day to day. If you're hungry, this role is a front-row seat to how a modern AI-driven services business is built, with a real path toward owning production, then our agent platform, then client-facing work.



## What you'll do



Client delivery management

- Own the production calendar across all active clients: what's in flight, what's due, what's blocked, and what's next for every account

- Triage and prioritize when multiple clients need something at once; make sensible calls on sequencing and escalate trade-offs early rather than letting something slip

- Build and maintain a working understanding of each client: their voice, their audience, their technical domain, their quality bar, and the feedback they've given before

- Feed that understanding back into the system (agent context, voice guides, QA checklists) so each client's quality bar is encoded rather than remembered

- Be the internal point of contact for "where are we on X for client Y"; the team should never have to chase you for status



Production

- Produce client content (blog posts, video support materials, dashboards) through our AI agents, working from clear briefs and context provided by our strategy team

- Run quality checks against client voice and our standards before work goes to review

- Keep the production pipeline moving: schedules tracked, deliveries on time, nothing slipping silently

- Support production of our own content, the same engine we sell, pointed at ourselves



Agent building and optimization

- Build new agents and workflows as our services expand: define the task, structure the context and instructions, test against real briefs, and iterate until output is reliably good

- Optimize existing agents: diagnose why output is weak (prompt, context, data, workflow), test fixes, and measure whether they worked

- Maintain the knowledge and context our agents run on (client voice guides, methodology, examples) so quality improves rather than drifts

- Document what you build so the rest of the team can use and extend it



Data and insight

- Keep our data systems fresh: client metrics updated weekly, event and market data accurate, gaps chased down and filled

- Review client and internal performance data on a regular cadence and spot trends, anomalies, and patterns before anyone asks

- Turn what you see into recommendations: a short, clear "here's what the data shows and here's what I'd do next" for the strategy team and, over time, for clients

- Monitor operational tripwires (missing metrics, stalled deliveries, quiet clients, degrading agent output) and alert the team with enough context to act



## What we require



- Proven ability to manage many concurrent workstreams. You've juggled multiple clients, projects, or stakeholders with competing deadlines and kept all of them on track, and you stay calm and systematic when everything is urgent

- A technical background. You've worked in or around the tech industry and are comfortable with how software products, developers, and technical teams operate. You should think like someone who has shipped software, whether or not you've written it

- Enough technical depth to understand what our clients do and who they sell to. You can read a client's product docs and grasp what a developer or DevOps engineer would care about, and you can tell when content misses that audience

- Hands-on experience with AI tools beyond casual use. You've built something with prompts, agents, automations, or LLM-based workflows, and you have opinions about what makes them work well or badly

- Data fluency. You're comfortable in spreadsheets and dashboards, you can read a chart and know what question to ask next, and you can explain a trend to someone in two sentences

- Excellent, fluent spoken and written English and a sharp eye for quality. You notice when something reads wrong

- Highly organized and self-directed. You build systems for tracking work rather than relying on memory, you keep many threads moving without being chased, and you surface problems before they become emergencies

- Smart, fast-learning, and hungry to grow. We weight trajectory over pedigree

- A bachelor's degree, or equivalent ability you can demonstrate (our work-sample test matters more than your CV)

- Reliable overlap with US Eastern mornings (roughly 8pm to 12am PHT) for team coordination; the rest of your day is flexible and async. You'll need to be flexible to join calls, sometimes early morning or in your evenings

- Based in the Philippines

- This will be your full-time job, no side gigs



## What will make you stand out



- Agency, consultancy, or client-services experience: you've served multiple accounts simultaneously and know what it feels like when they all need you on the same day

- You've built agents or multi-step LLM workflows using tools like Claude, OpenAI, LangChain, N8N, Zapier, Make, or custom code

- You can write or read basic scripts (Python, JavaScript, SQL), enough to automate a task or pull data yourself

- Experience with Google Analytics, Search Console, or similar analytics platforms, and a track record of turning that data into decisions

- Experience working with or marketing to technical audiences: developers, DevOps, security, data teams

- Experience in content marketing, SEO/GEO, or social media, especially in B2B tech

- You've worked at a startup, dev tools company, or agency serving tech clients



## How we hire



Short application, a conversation, then a paid work-sample brief. Real work, real pay, so we both find out what working together is actually like. The work sample will include producing something through an agent, improving the agent, interpreting a dataset, and working through a realistic multi-client prioritization scenario. We start with a 3-month contract at full salary, converting to permanent with a raise when it's working, and we'll be straight with you throughout about how it's going.

title: Part-Time Cold Caller - US Real Estate (Property Owner Outreach)
description:
I'm a US-based real estate broker looking for a reliable, well-spoken cold caller to contact property owners and find out whether they'd be interested in selling their building. You'll work directly with me.



WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Call property owners from lead lists I provide (no lead hunting needed)

- Have friendly, professional conversations to find out if the owner would consider selling, and gather key details (timeline, motivation, price expectations, best time for a follow-up)

- Qualify interested owners and hand them off to me with clear notes

- Log every call and outcome in our CRM (access and training provided)



SCHEDULE:

- Monday to Friday, 3-4 hours per day

- You choose your hours, any time between 8 AM and 5 PM US Pacific Time (about 12 AM - 9 AM Philippine Time; 11 PM - 8 AM during US daylight saving)



COMPENSATION:

- $400/month to start (part-time, 20 hrs/week), paid monthly

- $1,000 flat commission for every lead you hand off that closes as a sale within 12 months of your handoff - paid after closing, even if you are no longer working with me by then

- Starts with a 2-week paid trial



WHAT TO EXPECT:

This is a part-time role (20 hrs/week). It's my first time building this, so it's a new experiment for me and I can't guarantee how long it will last. If it's going well, I plan to review your pay after 6 months based on your results. I'd rather be upfront about all of that.



WHAT I PROVIDE:

- A US phone number and calling software (dialer)

- CRM access, lead lists, and a call script and training



REQUIREMENTS:

- Strong spoken and written English - clear, confident, easy to understand

- Quiet place to work with no background noise

- Reliable internet with a backup (mobile data or second connection)

- Computer and a good headset with a microphone



STRONGLY PREFERRED:

- Cold calling, telemarketing, or appointment-setting experience

- US real estate experience (wholesale, acquisitions, or investor calls)



HOW TO APPLY:

Start your application with the word GROUNDWORK, then:



1. Describe your cold calling experience - what were you calling about, for how long, and roughly how many calls per day?

2. Which hours (US Pacific Time) would you work, Monday to Friday?

3. Record a 1-minute voice clip (use the free Vocaroo voice recorder website, or a Google Drive link). Introduce yourself, then pretend you're calling a building owner and ask if they'd consider selling their property. Paste the link in your application.



I'll review your OnlineJobs profile for everything else, so make sure it's up to date.



Applications without GROUNDWORK, the 2 answers, and a voice link will not be reviewed.

title: Technical Recruiter (Remote)
description:
Role Overview



Barrister is seeking a motivated and proactive Technical Recruiter to join our

Technician Management & Deployment (TMD) division.

This is a high-volume, outbound recruiting role focused on identifying, screening, and

onboarding qualified field service technicians to support Barrister's nationwide service

requirements and Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

Success requires someone who is comfortable making a high volume of outbound calls,

engaging prospective technicians, evaluating technical qualifications, and consistently

moving candidates through the recruiting and onboarding pipeline.



Key Responsibilities



High-Volume Talent Acquisition:

Actively source and recruit qualified field service technicians using job boards, resume

databases, professional networks, referrals, internal resources, and cold outreach.



Candidate Screening:

Conduct telephone interviews to evaluate technical experience, field service

background, communication skills, tools, transportation, availability, geographic

coverage, and overall suitability for available opportunities.



Technical Assessment:

Identify technicians with experience in areas such as desktop and laptop support,

printers, point-of-sale equipment, networking, servers, hardware installation, equipment

replacement, break-fix service, and other IT field services.



Full-Cycle Recruitment:

Move qualified candidates through Barrister's recruiting and onboarding process,

including candidate qualification, testing or skills evaluation, required documentation,

background screening coordination, training, and orientation.



Deployment Support:

Work closely with internal Operations and Technician Assignment teams to understand

technician coverage gaps, open staffing requirements, client needs, and SLA priorities.



Pipeline Management:

Maintain accurate candidate records and recruiting activity within Barrister's recruitment

and tracking systems. Follow up consistently with candidates until they complete

onboarding or are removed from consideration.



Performance Accountability:

Meet established recruiting and productivity expectations, which may include outbound

call volume, talk time, candidate activity, technician identification, completed

onboarding, and assigned staffing objectives.



Qualifications



- Experience in high-volume recruiting, staffing, tele-sales, call center operations,

or outbound customer engagement.

- Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.

- Comfortable working in a high-volume Outbound calling environment.

- Strong telephone interviewing and candidate-engagement skills.

- Ability to work independently in a fully remote environment.

- Strong organizational and follow-up skills.

- Ability to manage multiple candidates, staffing requests, and priorities

simultaneously.

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced, metrics-driven and SLA-focused

environment.

- Strong computer skills and ability to work with web-based recruiting and tracking

systems.

- Previous IT staffing, technical recruiting, or field service recruiting experience is

strongly preferred.



Terms of Employment



Schedule: Full-Time, 40 hours per week. Work schedule will support Barrister's U.S.-

based operations.



Remote Work: This is a 100% remote position. Candidates must have a reliable

computer, stable high-speed internet connection, headset/telephone capability, and a

professional remote work environment.

title: Property Maintenance & Field Operations Supervisor / Manager
description:
Barrister Premier Properties, LLC

Mandeville / Covington — Northshore Louisiana



Barrister Premier Properties, LLC is seeking an experienced, hands-on Property Maintenance & Field Operations Supervisor / Manager to take ownership of maintenance and field operations across our portfolio of multifamily apartments, hotels, shopping centers, commercial properties, and tenant spaces throughout the Northshore.



We are looking for someone with strong construction and property maintenance experience who can diagnose problems, determine the correct repair solution, lead a 3–4 person in-house maintenance crew, manage work orders, procure materials, and personally perform or assist with repairs when needed.



Key Responsibilities



-Manage, assign, prioritize, and track daily maintenance work orders.

-Lead, supervise, and hold accountable a 3–4 person in-house maintenance crew.

-Diagnose building, construction, and maintenance issues and determine the appropriate repair solution.

-Create scopes of work, material lists, and basic material takeoffs.

-Purchase and stage materials ahead of scheduled work and respond quickly to emergency material needs.

-Perform hands-on repairs and maintenance alongside the crew when necessary.

-Conduct regular property walks and inspections to identify maintenance needs before they become larger problems.

-Perform tenant and resident move-out inspections and coordinate turnover work.

-Establish and maintain preventative maintenance schedules across the portfolio.

-Respond to emergency maintenance issues and prioritize work based on urgency, safety, property damage exposure, and operational impact.

-Track outstanding repairs and ensure work is completed properly, timely, and to company standards.

-Coordinate with outside subcontractors when work requires specialized trades or additional manpower.

-Verify completed work and maintain accountability for quality, materials, labor, and company resources.

-Take full ownership of maintenance issues from initial diagnosis through final completion.



Qualifications



-5+ years of experience in construction, property maintenance, facilities maintenance, or maintenance supervision.

-Strong working knowledge of multiple trades, including:

            -Carpentry and general construction

            -Plumbing

            -Electrical

            -HVAC

            -Drywall

            -Painting and finishes

-Proven ability to lead and manage maintenance or construction personnel.

-Experience preparing scopes of work, material takeoffs, and purchasing materials.

-Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving ability.

-Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple active work orders and properties simultaneously.

-Comfortable working in the field daily and performing hands-on work when required.

-Reliable transportation and a clean driving record.

-Strong communication skills and professional presence when interacting with tenants, residents, vendors, subcontractors, and company personnel.



Ideal Candidate



-We are looking for someone who is hands-on, dependable, organized, decisive, and accountable.

-The right candidate should be able to walk into a property, identify the problem, determine the appropriate solution, obtain the necessary materials, assign or perform the work, and make sure the job is completed correctly.

-You should be comfortable making decisions in the field, working under pressure, managing competing priorities, leading a crew, and treating company properties, materials, equipment, and resources as if they were your own.

-We want someone who does not simply identify problems or pass them along. We are looking for someone who takes ownership of the problem and drives it through completion.

-This position is critical to establishing and maintaining a reliable, organized, responsive, and accountable in-house property maintenance operation across the Barrister Premier Properties portfolio.

title: AI Utilization Expert (Claude & ChatGPT)

title: Head of finance
description:
About the Role



ConciergeMD is seeking a hands-on Head of Finance to oversee the company’s financial operations and support

profitable growth. Our services include concierge medicine, in-home medical care, memberships, and health

optimization treatments.



Reporting to the CEO and working closely with the Managing Director, this person will own financial reporting,

budgeting, cash flow management, accounting oversight, and profitability analysis. They will ensure leadership

has accurate financial information and clear recommendations to guide business decisions.

The ideal candidate is comfortable managing financial strategy while also reviewing transactions, resolving

discrepancies, and improving day-to-day processes.



Key Responsibilities



Financial Reporting & Accounting



● Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close, ensuring accurate and timely reporting.

● Prepare and review profit and loss statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements.

● Oversee bookkeeping, account reconciliations, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and payroll

coordination.

● Ensure revenue and expenses are recorded correctly and allocated to the appropriate services,

departments, and legal entities, where applicable.

● Manage relationships with external bookkeepers, accountants, and tax professionals.

● Establish clear financial procedures, reporting deadlines, and accountability.

Cash Flow & Budgeting

● Monitor cash balances and maintain a rolling cash flow forecast.

● Develop the annual budget and update forecasts as business needs change.

● Compare actual results against budget, explain variances, and recommend adjustments.

● Manage payment schedules to ensure sufficient cash for operating expenses and planned investments.

● Help leadership evaluate hiring, expansion, and major spending decisions.

Profitability & Financial Strategy

● Analyze profitability by service, membership tier, provider, and geographic market.

● Monitor provider compensation, laboratory and pharmacy costs, medical supplies, and other service

delivery expenses.

● Evaluate pricing, discounts, membership benefits, and subscriptions to ensure sustainable margins.

● Build financial models for new services, partnerships, and growth opportunities.

● Calculate and verify commissions, bonuses, and profit-sharing payments according to approved

agreements.

● Present a monthly financial dashboard with key results, risks, and recommended actions.

Billing & Revenue Management

● Oversee reconciliation of patient payments, memberships, subscriptions, refunds, chargebacks, and

payment processor deposits.

● Work with operations to identify missed charges, failed payments, outstanding balances, and billing

errors.

● Ensure prepaid services and membership revenue are accounted for appropriately.



● Improve billing and collections processes while supporting a positive patient experience.

Vendor & Expense Management

● Review vendor invoices and recurring expenses for accuracy, duplicate charges, and unnecessary

spending.

● Partner with operations to resolve billing discrepancies and disputed invoices.

● Monitor laboratory, pharmacy, provider, software, and other vendor costs.

● Identify cost-saving opportunities and support contract negotiations.

● Establish purchasing, reimbursement, and payment approval procedures with appropriate financial

controls.

Tax, Compliance & Systems

● Coordinate with external tax professionals to ensure required filings and payments are completed on

time.

● Maintain a calendar of financial, tax, and reporting deadlines.

● Support audits and other requests for financial documentation.

● Improve accounting systems and reporting workflows, including connections with billing, payment, and

payroll platforms.

● Maintain organized financial records and protect confidential information.

Qualifications

● 5+ years of progressive accounting or finance experience, including financial reporting, budgeting, and

cash flow management.

● Previous experience as a Head of Finance, Finance Director, Controller, or similar finance leader.

● Strong accounting knowledge and experience overseeing day-to-day financial operations.

● Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills and proficiency with accounting software.

● Ability to identify financial issues, investigate their causes, and implement practical solutions.

● Strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through.

● Ability to explain financial results clearly to non-finance team members.

● Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or a related field; CPA preferred.

● Experience in healthcare, concierge medicine, membership-based services, or a growing service

business preferred.

What Success Looks Like

● Accurate financial statements are delivered on a consistent monthly schedule.

● Leadership has clear visibility into cash flow, expenses, and profitability.

● Billing gaps and vendor discrepancies are identified and resolved promptly.

● Pricing and spending decisions are supported by reliable financial analysis.

● Financial processes are organized, documented, and able to support company growth.

First 90 Days



Review ConciergeMD’s financial records and processes, identify key gaps, establish a reliable monthly reporting

schedule, develop a cash flow forecast, and present a prioritized plan to strengthen financial controls and improve profitability.

Maxon AI Results | Remote



Maxon AI Results is looking for an experienced CRM specialist to organize and maintain our customer and prospect information in Less Annoying CRM (LACRM).



We help small and midsized businesses implement practical AI services, beginning with tools such as AI receptionists, missed-call follow-up, and appointment support. We need someone who can make sure every prospect and customer receives timely, organized follow-up—from the first inquiry through onboarding and ongoing service.



This is a hands-on CRM role. We’re looking for someone who has actually worked with Less Annoying CRM and can explain how they would set it up for a small service business.



Responsibilities



* Set up LACRM to track prospects, customers, follow-up tasks, and customer history.

* Create clear stages for new leads, contacted prospects, proposals, onboarding, active customers, support issues, and renewals.

* Import and organize contact information, check for duplicates, and keep records accurate.

* Record customer conversations, decisions, requests, and agreed next steps.

* Create and monitor reminders so prospects and customers receive follow-up on time.

* Help organize customer onboarding, including contact details, goals, project status, and next actions.

* Track customer questions or service issues and make sure they reach the right person.

* Prepare a short weekly report showing new prospects, follow-ups due, overdue tasks, active customers, and open issues.

* Write simple instructions explaining how the CRM is organized and how routine tasks should be handled.

* Recommend practical connections to tools such as
 or Mailchimp when appropriate. Do not add integrations or send campaigns without approval.



Qualifications



* Hands-on experience setting up and maintaining Less Annoying CRM.

* Strong record-keeping, organization, and follow-through.

* Good written and spoken English.

* Comfortable communicating professionally with U.S. small-business customers.

* Able to explain CRM choices in plain language.

* Careful with confidential customer information.

* Reliable internet and ability to provide a brief written progress report.



Initial paid trial



The selected candidate will complete a small paid trial using sample information only. The trial will include organizing sample contacts, setting up customer stages, creating follow-up tasks, and showing how a weekly customer-care report would work.



To apply



Please send:



1. A brief description of your LACRM experience.

2. Examples of CRM systems or workflows you have set up.

3. Your hourly or project rate and weekly availability.

4. A short explanation of how you would track a new prospect from first inquiry through ongoing customer service.

5. Two work references, if available.



Please do not send confidential information from former clients.

title: AI solutions implementation and ongoing technical support.for small to medium businesses.
description:
**REMOTE CONTRACT ROLE — PHILIPPINES PREFERRED**

**Senior AI Receptionist and Automation Implementation and ongoing technical support Specialist**

**Maxon AI Results**



Maxon AI Results is building a business that helps small and midsize companies improve their operations with practical AI solutions.. Our first service will be an AI receptionist that can answer calls, respond to common questions, capture and qualify leads, schedule appointments, and trigger reliable follow\-up\.



We’re seeking an exceptionally capable technical specialist to help us build, test, launch, and support this service\. You would first help us set up and operate the receptionist system for Maxon AI Results, then help us adapt it for customers\. Over time, you may also help us introduce additional AI products and services\.



This is a direct working relationship with the business owner\. We are not looking for an agency salesperson or a consultant who only makes recommendations\. We need a hands\-on professional who can deliver working systems, document them clearly, and support them after launch\.



**What you will do**



- Recommend and configure appropriate AI voice receptionist and telephony tools\.

- Build call flows for greeting callers, answering approved questions, capturing contact details, routing calls, taking messages, and scheduling appointments\.

- Connect the receptionist to calendars, CRM systems,
, forms, and automation tools as needed\.

- Configure missed\-call responses, follow\-up messages, appointment confirmations, and reminders\.

- Test realistic call scenarios, identify failures, and improve the caller experience\.

- Set up reporting so we can track call volume, missed calls, appointments, lead details, and system issues\.

- Maintain and troubleshoot systems after launch; explain problems and resolutions in plain language\.

- Document each setup so it can be maintained, reviewed, and adapted for customers\.

- Help us evaluate and add other practical AI services as the business grows\.

- Protect customer and company information through careful access controls and sound data\-handling practices\.



**Required qualifications**



- Demonstrated experience building and maintaining AI voice agents, virtual receptionists, or comparable production phone systems\.

- Strong hands\-on experience with telephony or contact\-center platforms and integrations\.

- Experience connecting systems through APIs, webhooks, automation platforms, or native integrations\.

- Experience working with calendars, CRMs, and appointment\-booking workflows\.

- Ability to troubleshoot call quality, routing, transcription, scheduling, and integration problems\.

- Strong written and spoken English; able to explain technical decisions clearly to a nontechnical owner\.

- Excellent documentation habits and dependable follow\-through\.

- Able to work remotely and provide regular overlap with U\.S\. business hours\.

- References, work samples, or a live demonstration of systems you personally built\.



**Strong advantages**



- Experience serving HVAC, plumbing, electrical, property\-management, or other local service businesses\.

- Experience with consent, call recording, privacy, and data\-retention settings for voice systems\.

- Experience with CRM setup, lead qualification, analytics, and customer onboarding\.

- Experience supporting multiple client accounts without mixing customer data or access\.



**Initial engagement**



The role is expected to begin as a paid, part\-time contract of approximately 20 hours per week\. We will agree on the exact schedule and compensation based on demonstrated experience and the proposed scope\. We are looking for a long\-term technical partner as the customer base grows\.



The selection process will include a paid practical assignment\. The assignment will ask you to design and demonstrate a basic receptionist workflow, document the setup, and explain how you would test it\. We will not ask for unpaid production work or access to sensitive customer data during the assessment\.



**How to apply**



Please send:



1. A brief introduction and your location and time zone\.

2. A résumé or summary of relevant experience\.

3. Links, screenshots, or a short video showing systems you personally built\.

4. The platforms you used and exactly what you implemented\.

5. A short explanation of how you would build a receptionist that answers calls, captures leads, schedules appointments, and sends reminders\.

6. Your hourly or monthly rate and availability\.

7. Two professional references, if available\.



Applications that only list tools without showing what you personally built will not be considered\.

title: Part-Time Appointment Setter (US Business Calls) - Roofing - Mon to Fri, 4 Hours a Day
description:
Grandma Roofer is a roofing company in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, Texas.

We help churches, property managers and building owners keep their

roofs in good shape.

We offer a free roof look with photos. Nothing up front.



THE JOB

You will phone business offices in Texas and set up a short, free

roof-look visit.

You are an appointment setter. Your only goal is to book the visit.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Make about 40 to 60 calls a day from a call list we give you.

- Use our short script. Stay on script.

- Ask who looks after the roofs at the building.

- Ask simple quote questions: roof size and type, any leaks, who makes

the decision, timeline, and budget window.

- Never give a price. Say: "Cindy gives prices after the free roof look."

- Offer two visit times. Book one.

- Log the result of every call in a Google Sheet (we give you the codes).

- Leave a short voi
 (live voice only) when nobody answers.

- Say "This call may be recorded" at the start of every call.

- If someone says "stop calling" or "do not call", log DNC right away.

- Send a short end-of-day summary in the sheet.



WHAT YOU WILL NOT DO

- No quoting prices. No selling. No taking payment.

- No promises or guarantees about the roof or the work.

- No claims about the company beyond the script.

- No texting or
ing prospects.

- No calling anyone not on your list.

- Book the visit only. The owner handles everything after that.



PAY

- $5 to $7 per hour, based on your voice test and phone screen. Paid

weekly or every two weeks.

- Plus $15 for every visit that is kept (the visit happens and we meet

the decision-maker).

- One-month trial. The first week is a paid trial at your hourly rate.

- We review your work every Friday. If it goes well, you continue.

- 4 hours a day, Monday to Friday. About 20 hours a week.

- No weekend calls.



SCHEDULE

- Monday to Friday, 4 hours a day.

- Calls are made between 9 AM and 5 PM Central Time (US).

- Starting block: 9 AM to 1 PM Central. That is 10 PM to 2 AM

Philippine time now, and 11 PM to 3 AM after US clocks change on Nov

1.

- If you cannot work these hours, please do not apply.



REQUIREMENTS

- Excellent, clear English. Native-level or near-native.

- Neutral, very light accent. Easy for Americans to understand on the phone.

- Upbeat, warm and friendly. We should hear your smile on the phone.

- REQUIRED: a 60-second voice recording reading the test script (see

"How to apply").

- REQUIRED: a short live phone screen if you are shortlisted.

- Quiet room. Good headset. Stable internet (wired is best).

- A laptop or desktop that runs Chrome.

- Comfortable making phone calls to businesses and hearing "no" politely.

- Reliable. You show up every shift.

- US call-center experience preferred (cold calling or appointment setting).



HOW TO APPLY (follow every step or we will skip your application)

1. Use the subject line: ROOF CALLER - [Your Name]

2. Answer the 5 questions below.

3. Attach (or link) a 60-second voice recording of the test script below.

4. Tell us your hourly rate and your available hours.

5. If shortlisted, be ready for a short live phone screen.



5 SCREENING QUESTIONS

1. Which US businesses have you called before, and what was your job?

(If none, say "none" and tell us why you would be good at this.)

2. A church secretary says, "We're not interested." What do you say

next? Write your exact words.

3. A property manager says, "What does it cost?" You may not quote

prices. What do you say? Write your exact words.

4. The person says, "Please stop calling me." What do you do?

5. This job is 9 AM to 1 PM Central, Monday to Friday. What are your

hours in the Philippines, and can you work them every day with a quiet

room and wired internet?



AUDIO TEST SCRIPT (read out loud, about 60 seconds, record it, one take is fine)

Say it the way you would on a real call. Smile. Speak slowly and clearly.



"Hi, this is [your first name], calling for Cindy at Grandma Roofer.

This call may be recorded.

Do you have a minute? I'll be quick.

We're giving churches and property managers in Benbrook a free roof

look with photos.

Who looks after the roofs at your building?

About how big is the roof, and what kind is it? Any leaks right now?

Is there a timeline or budget window you're working with?

Cindy gives prices after the free roof look.

Could we schedule a 20-minute visit? Nothing up front. We just leave

you the photos.

I have Tuesday at 10 AM, or Wednesday at 2 PM. Which works better?"



Then answer this one in your own words (10 seconds):

The person says: "We already have a roofer."



SHOW YOUR WORK (we listen for)

- Excellent, clear English with a neutral, light accent.

- Upbeat, warm and friendly, with a smile we can hear.

- Clear words and a friendly tone.

- Not too fast. Not reading like a robot.

- Smooth handling of "We already have a roofer."

- Quiet background. No echo.

• Build useful spreadsheets and dashboards.

• Use approved automation tools to reduce manual work.

• Create and maintain standard operating procedures.

• Experience building dashboards and improving processes.

• Demonstrated history of improving business processes.

Core Values

People First

Clear Communication

Relentless Consistency

Confident Ownership



Results — First 90 Days

• Daily execution dashboard operating at 95%+ accuracy.

• 95%+ of assigned commitments completed on time.

• Weekly financial reports delivered on schedule.

• Financial exceptions documented and assigned for resolution.

• At least 10 recurring workflows documented.

We want someone who creates clarity, identifies problems, improves systems, and gets important work done.



We measure success by the results you deliver and how much better the business operates because of your work.

FIXED WORK SCHEDULE: Must be willing and available to work Monday through Friday, following a fixed US Eastern Time (EST/EDT) schedule.



TIME TRACKING: Must be comfortable using company-required time-tracking software throughout working hours.



HIPAA COMPLIANCE: Must understand HIPAA regulations and demonstrate the ability to handle confidential patient information securely.



TECH-SAVVY: Must be proficient with computers, online communication tools, dental software, and remote working systems.



INDEPENDENT WORK: Must be able to work efficiently with minimal supervision while consistently meeting performance expectations.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



The selected candidate will be responsible for:



Patient Communication: Manage inbound calls, respond to patient inquiries, and maintain professional communication in English and Spanish.

Schedule Optimization: Maintain an organized daily appointment schedule, manage scheduling conflicts, and apply appropriate double-booking procedures when authorized.



Patient Follow-Ups: Proactively contact patients regarding upcoming appointments, missed visits, treatment follow-ups, and pending scheduling requirements.



Dental Insurance Verification: Verify patient insurance eligibility, coverage, benefits, and relevant financial information.

Laboratory Case Management: Coordinate and track dental laboratory cases, monitor expected delivery dates, and follow up on outstanding cases.

WORK ARRANGEMENT



Work Setup: 100% Remote / Work From Home



Employment Type: Full-Time



Workdays: Monday to Friday



Work Schedule: Fixed US Eastern Time Zone (EST/EDT)



Industry: US Dental Practice



Required Software: Dentrix



Required Languages: English and Spanish



FINAL REMINDER TO ALL APPLICANTS



PLEASE DO NOT APPLY IF:



You are not fluent in BOTH English and Spanish.



You speak Chavacano but are not fluent in Spanish.

You are unwilling to work US Eastern Time hours.

title: L1/L2 Support Technician - Infrastructure Hosting (Remote, 24/7 Shift)
description:
L1/L2 Support Technician - Infrastructure Hosting (Remote, 24/7 Shift)



FDC Servers runs bare metal, VPS, and network infrastructure for clients across North America, Europe, and Asia. Real hardware in real data centers, in more than thirty locations. When something breaks, a client is down, and the ticket stays with you until it's actually resolved.



That ownership is the core of the job. You pick up a problem, work out what's actually wrong, fix what you can reach, and hand off the rest with enough detail that nobody has to start over.



We're hiring across the L1 and L2 band. Where you land is set at offer, based on what you show us rather than on your last title. There's a real path between the two, and we move people on demonstrated capability rather than time in seat.



COMPENSATION: USD $1,200-$2,400/month, depending on experience. Full-time, 40 hours/week.

SCHEDULE: 24/7 shift rotation. Shift assigned on coverage need, weekend rotation included.

REPORTS TO: Support shift lead, with technical escalation to the FDC tech lead.



YOU DON'T NEED A HOSTING BACKGROUND

We care about what you can do more than where you learned it. Backgrounds that work well here:

- You run a homelab. Proxmox VE or ESXi on secondhand hardware, a NAS you built, services you self-host, a network you've segmented into VLANs because you wanted to.

- You've administered game servers, a community Minecraft or CS network, anything where real users noticed when it went down.

- You've worked NOC or field ops at an ISP or telco, and you know what packet loss looks like before a customer calls about it.

- You were the person at a small company who ended up owning the servers because nobody else would.

- You're self-taught, with no degree, and you've spent years reading documentation and breaking things in a VM.

- You came from a different field entirely and taught yourself this because it held your attention.



Our interview goes into detail on the work you describe, so what helps you most is depth you can talk through.



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO

- Diagnose and resolve problems across hardware, operating systems, and networking: disks and RAID, SMART data, NICs, BIOS and UEFI, IPMI and BMC access, PXE boot failures, throughput and packet loss, stability

- Handle Linux and Windows Server administration as part of resolving tickets, not as a separate specialty

- Run our automation rather than doing everything by hand. We've built self-service jobs in AWX for multi-site iperf3 throughput testing, NIC tuning, and boot diagnostics. You get execute access early.

- Scope and coordinate remote hands work with data center technicians, and verify it was done before you close anything.

- Write internal notes that let the next shift continue without re-investigating.

- Escalate with evidence: what you checked, what you found, what you already tried, and what you need.



At the L2 end of the band, add owning the harder tickets on your shift, being the person L1s bring a stuck problem to, holding remote hands coordination for the whole shift, and taking first pass on tickets nobody else has been able to close.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You read the whole thread before you reply. You verify a server is reachable before telling a client it's reachable, and you know a ping reply isn't that verification. When you spot something wrong next to the thing you were asked to fix, you flag it rather than leaving it for whoever finds it next. You can tell the difference between "I don't know" and "this isn't mine." You handle a frustrated client like a professional. And you're curious — that matters more to us than any certification.



TECHNICAL BASELINE (this is what we'll test)

- Linux command line. Comfortable diagnosing and working without looking up every command. This is the floor.

- Hardware. Disk types and interfaces, SMART attributes, RAID levels and controller behavior, NIC types, server components and how they fail.

- Networking fundamentals. IP addressing and subnetting, VLANs, the difference between ping, SSH, and application reachability, basic routing, reading latency and packet loss.

- Written English clear enough for direct client communication. We're reading for clarity, not for accent or polish.



NICE TO HAVE: Proxmox VE or VMware, WHMCS or comparable ticketing, tcpdump/Wireshark, Docker or Kubernetes basics, any scripting. Certifications are not required — we test the baseline directly.



HOW TO APPLY

Send a CV if you have one. If your CV doesn't show what you can actually do, send us something that does instead: a short writeup of your homelab or home network; something you automated, however small; or a war story — the worst outage or hardware failure you've dealt with, what you thought it was at first, and what it turned out to be. Two or three paragraphs is plenty.



HOW WE HIRE

A written screening exercise first, then a live technical interview. We tell you yes or no either way, with the reason.



Note: We only review applications from ID-verified OnlineJobs.ph accounts.

title: L1/L2 Support Operations Technician - Server Provisioning (Remote)
description:
L1/L2 Support Operations Technician - Server Provisioning (Remote)



FDC Servers runs bare metal infrastructure across more than thirty data centers in North America, Europe, and Asia. Before any server reaches a customer, it has to be built and proven: hardware detected and verified, disks sanitized, firmware checked, health validated under our automated pipeline. Hundreds of machines move through that pipeline every month, and every one that passes becomes sellable inventory the same week.



You'd be one of the technicians running it. Working through IPMI and BMC consoles, driving network boot and automated install flows, reading SMART data and hardware detection output, d
 whether a failure is a bad disk, a dead cable, a firmware mismatch, or a process problem, and moving each machine to a real disposition rather than letting it sit.



Everything is remote and internal-facing. There's no customer contact in this role. Your writing goes to teammates and engineers, so we care that your notes are clear and complete rather than polished.



We're hiring across the L1 and L2 band. Where you land is set at offer, based on what you show us rather than on your last title.



COMPENSATION: USD $1,000-$2,400/month, depending on experience. Full-time, 40 hours/week.

SCHEDULE: Shift-based, weekday-weighted with some weekend rotation.

REPORTS TO: FDC support operations, with a named mentor for your first 90 days.



THE PART OF THE JOB THAT MATTERS MOST

Running the pipeline is the job description. Finding the patterns is where the value is.



If the same wipe failure shows up three times in a week, we'd like to hear about it, with the evidence, before anyone asks. If a batch of machines from one vendor keeps failing hardware detection the same way, that observation is worth more to us than a hundred routine passes. The technicians who grow fastest here are the ones who notice, say something, and propose the fix.



That shapes what we measure. We look at machines moved to real outcomes and at patterns found, not at hours logged or actions taken. If a wipe keeps failing, we'd much rather you stop and ask why than retry it forty times, and you'll never be penalized for pausing to investigate. Making a problem disappear permanently is the most valuable thing you can do here, and it's what we notice at review time.



YOU DON'T NEED A DATA CENTER BACKGROUND

We care about what you can do more than where you learned it. Backgrounds that work well here:

- You run a homelab. Secondhand servers, a NAS you built, Proxmox VE or ESXi, machines you've flashed, bricked, and recovered.

- You've built or repaired PCs seriously: diagnosing dead boards, reading POST behavior, knowing why a machine won't boot.

- You've administered game servers or community infrastructure where real users noticed downtime.

- NOC, field tech, or repair bench experience at an ISP, telco, or shop.

- Self-taught, with no degree, having learned by breaking things in a VM and reading documentation. That works. We test skills rather than paperwork.



TECHNICAL BASELINE (this is what we test)

- Hardware. Server components and how they fail. Disk types and interfaces, SMART attributes and what predicts failure, RAID basics, memory and thermal faults, BIOS and UEFI configuration.

- Boot and management planes. IPMI or equivalent BMC access, console redirection, network boot fundamentals (what has to happen between power-on and an OS installer starting).

- Linux command line. Comfortable reading logs, running diagnostics, following a runbook precisely, and knowing when what you're seeing means the runbook doesn't apply.

- Written English clear enough for a teammate to act on. This is not a customer-facing role, and accent or polish plays no part in the screen.



NICE TO HAVE: PXE/DHCP/network-boot troubleshooting, firmware update experience on NICs/drives/BMCs, any scripting, Ansible exposure or curiosity about it. Certifications aren't required - we test the baseline directly.



WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU APPLY

This isn't piecework, and volume of activity on its own isn't what gets noticed here. We can see the difference between forty retries and one diagnosis, and it's the diagnosis we reward. The role does ask you to speak up when something looks wrong, including when nobody has asked you.



HOW TO APPLY

Send a CV if you have one. Then send the thing that really gets our attention, one of: a description of your homelab or bench (what's in it, what broke, how you figured out why); a war story - the worst hardware problem you've chased, what you thought it was, and what it turned out to be; or something you automated or scripted, however small. Two or three paragraphs is plenty.



HOW WE HIRE

A written screening exercise first, then a live technical interview with scenario questions about real failures. "I don't know, here's how I'd find out" is a good answer here. We tell you yes or no either way, with the reason.



Note: We only review applications from ID-verified OnlineJobs.ph accounts.

title: L2/L3 Support Engineer - Infrastructure Hosting (Remote, Senior)
description:
L2/L3 Support Engineer - Infrastructure Hosting (Remote, Senior)



FDC Servers runs bare metal, VPS, and network infrastructure across more than thirty locations in North America, Europe, and Asia. Real hardware, real clients, and real consequences when it goes down.



This role is the end of the line on the technical side. When a ticket has been through two people and still isn't solved, it comes to you. When a client's packet loss doesn't show up in any obvious place, you're the one who finds it. When the same failure has happened four times, you're the one who works out why and makes it stop.



It's the depth track rather than the management track. You'll mentor and you'll set the technical standard, but nobody is asking you to run a rota or write performance reviews.



We're hiring across the L2 and L3 band. Level is set at offer based on what you demonstrate.



COMPENSATION: USD $2,200-$3,000/month, depending on experience. Full-time, 40 hours/week.

SCHEDULE: Shift-based with coverage expectations, weekend rotation shared across the team. More scheduling flexibility than our L1/L2 roles.

REPORTS TO: FDC support tech lead.



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO

- Own the problems nobody else could close. Intermittent packet loss, hardware that fails only under load, boot failures with no obvious cause, performance problems that aren't where the client thinks they are.

- Diagnose at the network layer and interpret what you find. MTR analysis, packet capture, DHCP and PXE failure signatures, routing behavior, throughput testing across sites.

- Turn one-off fixes into permanent ones: a runbook, a KB article, or an AWX job template so the L1s solve it themselves next time. We measure this.

- Build and extend the tooling. We run automation in AWX and Ansible: multi-site iperf3 throughput testing, NIC tuning, PXE boot diagnostics with packet-level tracing, firmware version tracking. You'll add to them.

- Set the technical standard by example. Your notes, escalations, and client writing are what the L1s copy.

- Be the second pair of eyes on remote hands scope before a technician drives to a data center.

- Escalate outward when it really is beyond us: vendor escalation, network team, hardware RMA, with the evidence assembled.



YOU DON'T NEED A HOSTING BACKGROUND, AND YOU MAY NOT NEED THE TITLE EITHER

We're looking for demonstrated depth, not a specific job history, and we're not counting years. Backgrounds that work well here:

- NOC or ISP engineering. If you've chased packet loss across a transit provider's network, you already do the hardest part of this job.

- A serious homelab or self-hosted setup. Multiple hypervisors, a segmented network, BGP at home because you wanted to understand it.

- You were the whole IT department somewhere. Everything from the switch config to the backups was yours.

- Open source or community work. You maintain something, you answer hard questions in a forum or 
.

- Adjacent engineering: SRE, DevOps, systems, platform. The hardware is learnable. The diagnostic instinct is the hard part.

- Self-taught, with no degree and no certs. That works. We test directly.



If you're strong but have never held a senior title because the org never had one to give you, please apply. That's a common shape and it isn't a mark against you.



TECHNICAL BASELINE (this is what we test)

- Linux, deeply. Not just navigating. Diagnosing: what's consuming the resource, why the service won't start, what the kernel is complaining about, and how to prove it.

- Networking, properly. Routing, VLANs, MTU and fragmentation, reading an MTR and knowing what asymmetry means, packet capture and analysis, DHCP and PXE mechanics. BGP concepts a strong plus.

- Hardware failure modes. SMART data and what predicts failure, RAID controller behavior, NVMe/SAS/SATA differences that matter in practice, memory and thermal faults, IPMI and BMC.

- Automation. Scripting at minimum. Ansible, or the ability to pick it up quickly.

- Written English strong enough to be the escalation standard. You'll write the notes other people learn from.



NICE TO HAVE: Proxmox VE at scale, Kubernetes/Docker/Ceph, runbooks or KB material others actually used, data center operations exposure, any language beyond scripting.



WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU APPLY

This isn't a step into meetings, and it isn't a role where you stop touching tickets. A large part of it is making yourself less necessary: writing down what you know and automating what you repeat, so the team can solve next time what you solved this time.



HOW TO APPLY

Send a CV. Then send us something that shows depth, because a CV usually doesn't. Any one of: a war story with the diagnostic path (a hard problem, what you thought it was, what the evidence said, how you proved the real cause - the wrong turns are the interesting part); something you built (a tool, script, playbook, repo, or homelab you can describe in detail); or something you wrote (a runbook, postmortem, KB article, or long technical answer).



HOW WE HIRE

A written technical exercise, then a live interview that goes deep on real scenarios rather than trivia. "I don't know, here's how I'd find out" is a good answer here. We tell you yes or no either way, with the reason.



Note: We only review applications from ID-verified OnlineJobs.ph accounts.

description:

ABOUT THE ROLE

This role is not for basic prompt-and-pray creators. We need someone who can execute the most intricate, complex AI workflows in the industry—from generating hyper-realistic AI UGC showing products being actively applied, worn, or interacted with, to seamlessly blending synthetic elements into live-action footage so they are entirely indistinguishable from reality.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Ultra-Realistic AI UGC & Product Interaction: Create flawless AI characters and UGC creators that look, move, and speak with human realism. Execute complex interactions such as applying skincare/products, unboxing, wearing items, and handling objects with zero physical artifacts.

Character, Voice, & Lip-Sync Mastery: Direct and manage hyper-realistic AI talking heads, precise lip-syncing, emotional delivery, and nuanced accent distinction (British/American).



End-to-End Post-Production: Handle scripting support, prompt engineering, compositing, upscaling (Topaz), sound design, colour grading, pacing, and final export delivery across Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or CapCut Desktop.



REQUIRED TECHNICAL SKIC-K (YOUR STACK)

AI Video: Runway Gen-3 / Gen-4, Kling, Luma Dream Machine, LTX Studio, or equivalent advanced motion models.



Voice / Character: HeyGen, ElevenLabs, D-ID, or custom pipeline equivalents.



Image Generation: Midjourney v6+, Leonardo.ai, Stable Diffusion (ControlNet/IP-Adapter for product consistency).

description:

HOW TO APPLY

 with the subject line "Probate Litigation Paralegal Application: [Your Name]" and include:

2. Cover letter describing your probate and probate litigation experience as it relates to this role

3. Expected hourly rate or salary range

4. Available start date



ABOUT BAY LEGAL, PC



Bay Legal, PC is a full-service California law firm combining expert legal counsel with modern technology to deliver seamless, results-driven representation.



POSITION OVERVIEW



We are seeking a highly skilled and detail-oriented Probate Litigation Paralegal / Legal Assistant with direct experience in a California law firm. This role focuses on contested probate, trust, and estate matters, and we are specifically looking for candidates who have supported attorneys through the full life of a probate litigation case, from the initial petition through discovery, hearings, mediation, and settlement or trial. The ideal candidate holds a law degree, is a currently practicing attorney, or brings extensive hands-on paralegal experience in California probate litigation.



PROBATE LITIGATION EXPERIENCE (REQUIRED)



California probate litigation experience is required. Experience with probate matters in other states is a plus and will be considered alongside it. Relevant experience includes:



- Will and trust contests

- Petitions under Probate Code Section 850 (including Heggstad petitions) and petitions for instructions

- Petitions to remove or suspend trustees, executors, or administrators

- Breach of fiduciary duty and trust accounting disputes, including objections to accountings

- Financial elder abuse claims connected to estates or trusts

- Contested conservatorships and guardianships

- Creditor claims, spousal and domestic partner property petitions, and heirship disputes



We also value experience with uncontested probate administration, including petitions for probate, Letters, Notices of Proposed Action, inventories and appraisals with the probate referee, creditor notices, and petitions for final distribution.



REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS



- Law degree (JD or foreign law degree) OR currently practicing attorney OR minimum 4 years of substantive paralegal experience in a California law firm

- Minimum 4 years of probate or probate litigation experience within a California law firm

- Working knowledge of the California Probate Code, California Rules of Court, and local probate rules

- Experience preparing and filing Judicial Council probate forms and California court e-filing

- Hands-on experience with Lawmatics and Clio Manage

- Paralegal certificate from an ABA-approved program preferred

- Strong written and verbal communication skills

- Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple cases and deadlines at the same time

- Reliable internet connection and home office setup for remote work



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



- Draft first-pass probate petitions, objections, responses, declarations, and proposed orders from firm templates for attorney review.

- Prepare and file Judicial Council probate forms, notices of hearing, and proofs of service with California superior courts.

- Monitor probate notes and tentative rulings, and help clear defects before hearing dates.

- Track and calendar statutory and court deadlines, including trust contest periods, hearing dates, continuances, and discovery deadlines.

- Prepare discovery requests and responses, deposition notices, and subpoenas for records, and organize documents received.

- Gather and organize evidence such as bank records, estate planning documents, medical records, and asset information for attorneys.

- Prepare and review fiduciary accountings and supporting schedules, and flag discrepancies for attorney review.

- Assist with mediation and settlement preparation, including briefs, exhibits, and settlement agreements.

- Assist with trial preparation, including exhibit lists, witness lists, and trial binders.

- Conduct factual research on estate assets, property records, court dockets, and public records, subject to attorney review.

- Conduct client intake interviews and gather case information under attorney supervision.

- Communicate professionally with clients, beneficiaries, heirs, courts, probate examiners, court investigators, and opposing counsel.

- Manage and update case files, deadlines, and client records in practice management systems (Lawmatics, Clio Manage, etc.).

- Coordinate execution, notarization, and e-signatures on legal documents.

- Draft, review, and proofread legal documents and correspondence, keep accurate records of all case activities, and maintain contemporaneous time records.
